summary: Gyurme Dorje worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA at the University of Edinburgh and his PhD at SOAS under Philip Denwood, alongside traditional teachers. He held a fellowship at SOAS (1991–1996) and translated for Tsadra Foundation (2007–2020).
Gyurme Wosel studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

György Kara worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Gyula Németh, Lajos Ligeti, and Barnabás Csongor. He served at ELTE, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and Indiana University Bloomington (1993–2022).

Gérard Colas specializes in Indology and religious studies. He held posts as Directeur de recherche at the CNRS (attested 2004) and the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (attested 2012).

Gérard Fussman specialized in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure from around 1960 to 1964 and became a professor at the Collège de France in 1984, succeeding Jean Filliozat.
Gérard Huet works in computational linguistics and Indology. He studied under George Ernst and Maurice Nivat, and served as a professor at Inria from around 1974.

Géza Bethlenfalvy worked in Tibetology and Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University under Lajos Ligeti, later holding posts at the University of Delhi (1970), Eötvös Loránd University, the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Vienna (2007–2008).

Gösta Liebert specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Lund University and the University of Gothenburg under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils M. Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He served as professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit at Gothenburg from 1955 to 1982.

Götz von Selle worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen, and later served at Göttingen and as professor and library director at the University of Königsberg (~1928–1945).

Günter Grönbold specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served at the Bavarian State Library from around 1975 to 2008, where he headed the Oriental Section from approximately 1988 to 2008.

Günter Schweiger is a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Gert Klingenschmitt and at Vienna University of Economics and Business. He served as a full university professor at Vienna University of Economics and Business (1974–2009).

H. Craig Melchert is a linguist who studied at Michigan State University and Harvard University (~1972–1977). He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and the University of California, Los Angeles (2007–2015).

H. G. Narahari specialized in Indology. He studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras under Chittenjoor Kunhan Raja, and held research posts at Madras and the Adyar Library and Research Centre (both attested 1944).

H. G. Quaritch Wales was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He studied at Cambridge and earned a PhD at SOAS under Charles Otto Blagden. He served as Field Director for the Greater India Society (~1934–1941).
H. V. Nagaraja Rao works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).

Hae-ju Sunim is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She served as a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and as an associate professor of Buddhist studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at Peking University under Jin Kemu and Zhongxin Jiang, and served as Director at the University of Freiburg in 2010.

Hajime Kitamura was a linguist and Tibetologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tokan Tada and held posts at the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), Reitaku University (president, 1986), and the Toyo Bunko (1958; 1990–2001).

Hajime Nakamura was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Hakuju Ui at the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at Tokyo (1954–1973) and founded and directed the Eastern Institute and Toho Gakuin.

Hajime Okayama was a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Peking University under Xianlin Ji, and CASS. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo from 1995 to 2012.
